issues.failure_explanation: Definition 4.3 only places R(T)_{2j} and R(T)_{2j+1} in [t_j,t_{j+1}). Hence t^{k+1}_{2j+2} lies in [t^k_{j+1},t^k_{j+2}), so [t^{k+1}_{2j},t^{k+1}_{2j+2}) is not contained in [t^k_j,t^k_{j+1}) for general admissible R, for example the dual parameterization (shift h/4). The two ends of the interval can use different pieces of the piecewise-average curve. The one-piece application of the boundedness property is therefore not justified. It is valid only when t^{k+1}_{2j+2}=t^k_{j+1}, as in the primal case.

The hypothesis therefore does not imply the next level, and the base case k=1 also leaves out r=2. issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 4.9 needs a set D' with W(D') in D' on which contractivity holds. The proof gives contractivity only on {P in D: delta(P)<=nu}. It shows delta(W^{kL}P)<=delta(P), which is control at multiples of L only. For L>1 nothing bounds delta(W^r P), 0<r<L, by nu. W is not assumed to be Lipschitz-like, and D-S controls only even-indexed points. The contraction estimate cannot be applied to the intermediate iterates W^r P, so the set is not shown invariant and Theorem 4.9 is misapplied.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, note that the power of $\eta$ scales like $\cdot/L$ with respect to the number of refinements.

issues.failure_explanation: Applied to S_1^{L_1}, Definition 6.1 gives the bound E*eta^{j+1} along blocks of L_1 steps. For level l-L_1 = j*L_1 the bound is E*eta^{l/L_1}, not E*eta^{l-L_1+1}. The proof uses the stronger single-step exponent. After multiplying by 2^l for divided differences, the error term is (2*eta^{1/L_1})^l. It decays only if eta<2^{-L_1}, whereas order 1 only gives eta<1/2. For L_1>1 the choice alpha=max{2 eta, mu_1}<1 is therefore unjustified and the Cauchy argument breaks. The same exponent slip in (delta_S1P) of Theorem 6.2 is harmless, since the final bound alpha^{floor(l/L)} survives.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis for L_1>1 to eta<2^{-L_1} (or define order-1 proximity of S^{L_1} with this scaling), and redo the recursion with exponent floor(l/L_1).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 6.5 is established only for L_1=1, which covers the application in Lemma 6.7. For L_1>1 the claimed C^1 conclusion is not proved under the stated hypothesis.
issues.title: C^1 theorem: proximity exponent for S_1^{L_1} is misread, which fails for L_1>1
issues.why_classification: Contained reformulation of the hypothesis with a re-derived recursion; the L_1=1 case and the example survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is worth noting that a subdivision scheme $S$ with a first-order contractivity factor, which also satisfies the D-S property, is $C^1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem 6.2 needs a displacement bound for the sequence being refined, here the divided differences D_l=(Delta S_1^l P)/2^{-l}. That is, d(D_{l+1,2j}, D_{l,j}) <= C*delta(D_l), the second-difference size. Theorem 6.5 assumes only first-order contractivity and proximity, and nothing about D-S for divided differences. D-S of the point sequence does not imply it: the divided-difference sequence is 2^l Delta of the points, and closeness of even points to the coarse points says nothing about differences. Without it, contraction of second differences does not give a Cauchy sequence of divided differences, since the level can drift as in Issue 5. The sentence on D-S plus first-order contractivity implying C^1 is unsupported for the same reason.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Omega \subset \R^n$ be a complete Riemannian manifold and let $\D \subseteq \Omega^\Z$.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma is stated for all points and a single C, within a setting of arbitrary complete embedded Riemannian manifolds. It fails without bounded geometry. Take Omega = graph of y=sin(x^2) in R^2, which is complete. Its curvature equals 4x^2 at points where cos(x^2)=0. For two nearby points there, the geodesic midpoint deviates from the chord midpoint by about kappa*|p_0-p_1|^2/8. So the best constant grows like x^2 and no uniform C exists. The cited estimate holds only with a constant depending on a compact region or curvature bound.
